- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to overshoot in bullish periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially < -0.5) — model fails to capture downside risk.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days — adjust for recent sentiment shifts or price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes, model overreacts and forecasts continued rise — cap forecast growth after +10% spike.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after strong upward moves — reduce forecast by 5–10% if recent 5-day avg is above 3σ.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.5), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecasts with 3-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates downside risk in low-sentiment periods — add 2–5% buffer if sentiment < -0.3 for 3+ consecutive days.
